seo.description: Guía de Rabat: Kasba de los Udayas, Torre Hassan, Chellah, medina, marina del Bouregreg y playa atlántica.

name: Rabat
hero_subtitle: Capital atlántica de Marruecos — acantilados de la kasba, Torre Hassan, Chellah y frente del Bouregreg.

info.area_val: Historic walls, red brick and Bouregreg calm

overview.title: A capital you can still explore on foot
overview.p1: Rabat sits where the Bouregreg meets the Atlantic: the white-and-blue Kasbah of the Udayas above the estuary, the unfinished Hassan Tower and Mausoleum of Mohammed V, the Roman–Merinid ruins of Chellah, and an old medina easier than Fez or Marrakech. An orderly, green political capital kept from feeling purely administrative by ocean breeze and estuary light.
overview.p2: One to three days cover the kasbah, Hassan complex, Chellah, the old medina and a walk on the marina or beach. Day trips to Salé across the river, Casablanca or the coast toward Kenitra. Choose a stay near the medina, Hassan or Agdal according to the atmosphere you prefer.

places.title: Places to visit in Rabat
places.subtitle: Kasbah, tower, necropolis, old medina and Bouregreg shore.

oudayas.title: Kasbah of the Udayas
oudayas.desc: White-and-blue quarter above the estuary with Andalusian gardens.

hassan.title: Hassan Tower
hassan.desc: Famous Almohad minaret and unfinished mosque square.

mausoleum.title: Mausoleum of Mohammed V
mausoleum.desc: Marble and zellige landmark beside Hassan Tower.

chellah.title: Chellah
chellah.desc: Roman and Merinid necropolis in a fortified garden above the Bouregreg.

medina.title: Rabat Old Medina
medina.desc: Compact lanes, souks and walls toward the ocean.

gardens.title: Andalusian Gardens
gardens.desc: Shady gardens inside the Kasbah of the Udayas.

marina.title: Bouregreg Marina
marina.desc: Modern marina and promenade opposite Salé.

beach.title: Rabat Beach
beach.desc: Atlantic sand under the walls and along the corniche.

museum.title: Rabat Museums
museum.desc: Archaeology and modern collections in the capital.

itinerary.title: Programa sugerido de 3 días
itinerary.subtitle: Kasbah and Hassan first, then Chellah and the waterfront.

detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Mañana — Kasba de los Udayas y Jardines
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Kasba de los Udayas y jardines andaluces — hermosas vistas sobre el Bouregreg y el Atlántico.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Explora los callejones de la medina, la calle de los Cónsules y una pausa de café cerca de las murallas históricas.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Contempla el atardecer desde una terraza de los Udayas y luego una cena marroquí en la medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Visita la plaza de la Torre Hassan y el mausoleo de mármol de Mohamed V.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Recorre las ruinas y jardines romano-meriníes de Chellah y descubre la historia del lugar.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Paseo nocturno por la marina del Bouregreg o cena en un restaurante con vistas al río.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Visita museos o cruza en barca tradicional hacia la ciudad vieja de Salé.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Tarde — Playa de Rabat y Corniche
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Relájate en la playa de Rabat o la corniche con tiempo libre en los cafés modernos de Agdal.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Disfruta de un último té de menta en la kasba o una cena frente al estuario.

stays.title: Where to stay in Rabat? Our favourites
stays.subtitle: Hotels near Hassan Tower and the kasbah, a practical base in Agdal, and a riad in the old medina.

card1.name: Hotel Tour Hassan
card1.desc: Classic address near Hassan Tower and the administrative centre — elegant rooms and a central base for the monuments.

card2.name: Hotel Oudaya
card2.desc: Stay close to the Kasbah of the Udayas and the Bouregreg — practical for the historic waterfront.

card3.name: Agdal Hotel
card3.desc: Modern hotel in Agdal — cafés, shops and train links nearby.

card4.name: Riad Dar El Menzeh
card4.desc: Charming riad inside the old medina walls offering authentic Moroccan hospitality and a quiet atmosphere.

booking_banner.title: Explore every stay in Rabat
booking_banner.desc: Compare live prices, read traveller reviews and discover more riads and hotels.

eat.title: Where to eat in Rabat
eat.subtitle: Old-medina tajines, kasbah tea, family tables and Atlantic seafood.

dinarjat.title: Restaurant Dinarjat
dinarjat.desc: Elegant Moroccan cooking in a restored medina house — tajines, pastilla and a classic Rabat address.

imprevu.title: L’Imprévu
imprevu.desc: Popular tables in the city centre and a varied menu — reliable stop between museums and the old medina.

naji.title: Dar Naji
naji.desc: Generous Moroccan dishes and a lively atmosphere — tajines and salads, a local and family favourite.

goeland.title: Le Goéland
goeland.desc: Atlantic fish and seafood near the water — Rabat classic for simple grills.

ty.title: Dar Zaki
ty.desc: Warm old-medina house for home-style couscous and tajines — simple, warm and family-friendly.

maure.title: Café Maure
maure.desc: Mint tea and pastries on kasbah terraces with a river view — not to miss.

1.title: Getting around
1.desc: The centre is easily walkable. Petit taxis for longer hops; private driver for Chellah. Tram links Rabat and Salé.

2.title: Calm Atlantic capital
2.desc: Quieter souks and fewer ticketed monuments — atmosphere is the main draw.

3.title: Heat on the walls
3.desc: Rampart walks have little shade. Morning and late afternoon are kinder.

daytrips.title: Day trips from Rabat
daytrips.subtitle: Across the Bouregreg, further along the coast or inland.

sale.name: Salé
sale.desc: Medina and beach right across the Bouregreg — tram or boat.

casa.name: Casablanca
casa.desc: About an hour by train — Hassan II Mosque and corniche.

kenitra.name: Kenitra & Mehdia
kenitra.desc: Coast and lagoon north of the capital.

q1.question: How many days in Rabat?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the main monuments; three allow Salé, museums or a quieter afternoon on the beach.

q2.question: Worth it compared with Marrakech?
q2.answer: Yes if you want a calmer capital, sea air, major monuments and less crowded souks.

q3.question: Airport code?
q3.answer: RBA (Rabat-Salé). Casablanca CMN is an alternative with more flights, then train to Rabat.

q4.question: Best area to stay?
q4.answer: Medina/Udayas for atmosphere, Hassan for the monuments, Agdal for modern cafés and space.
